spans.text: ...After meeting up with Persica, Kryuger directs the Doll squads to begin moving the neural cloud servers.
The original plan was to avoid the enemies using the Factory's elevators, but the continuous explosions have blocked their path.
The omnipresent enemies and the severe damage to the friendly squads make every decision of Kryuger's a vital one.
As Kryuger decides their next move, the Doll squads stop in the Factory to rest.
Thanks to Persica's tinkering, the neural cloud servers are much less of a load on the Dolls, but it is still a very heavy one for the current Doll squads.
Helian scrolls worriedly though the Dolls' statuses on her tablet as she walks toward Persica, who is sitting on the ground and drinking coffee.
Persica, is there a way to lighten the servers more?
Persica is so mad that she spits out her coffee.
What the hell are you saying? How could I finish software and hardware applicability tests, data compression, device remov—
Stop complaining. Just get to the point.
No, there isn't! Unless you move the servers back and give me half a month to optimize them!
Oh, and I'll need someone on full-time coffee-brewing duty for me—
Helian sighs and walks over to Kryuger.
Mr. Kryuger, given our current situation, I believe it is impossible to move the neural cloud servers away.
Should we consider Persica's suggestion and return the neural cloud servers—
Helian, do you remember your first mission after joining the Griffin base?
...Yes.
Back then, the Griffin base was only a year old or so, and Doll mercenaries were a rare thing.
All of society was watching us unblinkingly, looking forward to us making fools of ourselves.
Yes, back then people still couldn't accept human mercenaries being replaced by Dolls.
Your very first mission was to lead a squad of Dolls into the contaminated zones to recover supplies.
Entering the contaminated zones was already extremely risky to begin with, and the first-gen Tactical Dolls was nowhere as efficient as they are now.
But I didn't disgrace Griffin, and the success of the mission even dealt those naysayers a tight slap.
Haha... Yes, no matter how much you cried or how much stress you were under, you grit your teeth and completed the mission.
Mr. Kryuger... Why are you bringing up such ancient history...?
To me, it feels like it happened yesterday.
And now, we are at another turning point.
Once again, Griffin's future is in our hands.
...I understand.
Helian gazes at the Dolls working around her.
We'll make it through as well this time.
... Carter's fingers drum rhythmically on the table.
Haven't you found the objective yet?
We've taken the whole of Basement 1, but we haven't found any traces of humans.
Griffin has taken more than 50% Doll casualties so far. This is a very good start.
Don't let up. Press the attack.
Understood.
Remember at all times that Kryuger is a monster who strikes back the moment he can catch his breath.
That is his strength, but if you can make use of it, it can also become a fatal weakness.
Yes sir! I will inform the men.
The Spetsnaz officer returns to his post and the battle zone inside the Griffin base.
Carter's gaze turns to the floorplan of the Griffin base and the Doll count.
Now how will you turn this around, Kryuger?
